intro: Professionals and everyday users convert kilojoules (kJ) to kilocalories (kcal) when working across metric and other standards in residential electricity billing, HVAC heating load calculations, battery storage sizing, and nutritional energy tracking. One kilojoule equals 0.239006 kilocalories, while 1 kilocalorie (food calorie) equals 4.184 kilojoules. Whether you are verifying energy specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Dietary Calories (kcal) vs. Chemistry Gram Calories (cal)
items: On nutrition labels, a capitalized "Calorie" (Cal) is actually 1 kilocalorie (1,000 small gram calories = 4,184 Joules).

In physics and chemistry lab equations, 1 small calorie (cal) is the energy required to warm 1 gram of water by 1 °C (4.184 J). Always check whether your source means dietary kcal or thermochemical cal.

faqs.question: How many kilocalories (kcal) are in 1 kilojoule (kJ)?
faqs.answer: There are 0.23900574 kilocalories (kcal) in 1 kilojoule (kJ), which rounds to 0.239 kcal for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 kilocalorie (food calorie) equals 4.184 kilojoules.

faqs.question: How do I convert kilojoules to kilocalories (kJ to kcal)?
faqs.answer: To convert kilojoules to kilocalories, use the formula: kcal = kJ × 0.23900574. For example, converting 500 kJ gives 119.5029 kcal.

faqs.question: What is 500 kilojoules in kilocalories?
faqs.answer: 500 kilojoules (kJ) equals exactly 119.5029 kilocalories (kcal) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
